blocks.h: How a pure steam generator works
blocks.caption: Feed is preheated and vented to strip air and carbon dioxide (CO₂). The evaporator boils it behind a double tube sheet; a separator returns droplets, and their endotoxin, to the evaporator. Blowdown removes concentrate.

blocks.h: Questions validation and engineering teams ask

items.q: You are a new firm. How do you back your FAT and SAT results?
items.a: With evidence you can check: a FAT protocol your quality unit approves, a witnessed test on steam, calibrated test instruments with certificates in the report, and the raw readings in the executed protocol. At SAT we test steam quality at the sterilizer, where EN 285 is judged, not only at the generator.

items.q: What if our steam fails EN 285 at the sterilizer?
items.a: Usually the header is the cause: condensate in sagging runs, failed traps, damaged insulation or dead legs gives wet steam from a generator that tests dry. We size both together, so it is ours to find. We test at generator and sterilizer, correct the header and retest. [header retest included or quoted separately]

items.q: Does the condensate really have to meet WFI?
items.a: For steam that sterilizes materials or product-contact surfaces directly, yes: Annex 1, 6.17 asks for condensate that meets the current WFI monograph, without microbial testing. USP applies its < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin limit when the steam is used to make parenterals. Steam that only heats jackets or coils can be plant steam; your contamination control strategy says which users are which.

items.q: EN 285 is a European sterilizer standard. Does it apply to us?
items.a: Annex 1, which Health Canada applies as GUI-0119 since 1 April 2024, names gases, dryness and superheat but sets no numbers. Most sites and sterilizer manufacturers use the EN 285 values. If your sterilizer manufacturer specifies different limits, we design to the stricter of the two.

items.q: How often do we have to test?
items.a: Annex 1 asks for regular representative sampling and periodic assessment of the physical parameters, with no interval. A common approach: condensate chemistry and endotoxin quarterly, non-condensable gases quarterly until data support longer, dryness annually, superheat watched continuously from pressure and temperature. Your validation plan sets the frequency.

items.q: Does an imported generator need a Canadian registration number?
items.a: Yes. Pressure vessels and fittings installed in Canada need a CRN under CSA B51 from the province of installation, and a generator designed for another market may need design changes first. We put registration in the schedule from the start. [Aquemi CRN process and provinces covered]
